thesis: Material constraints do not determine distribution, merit or an inevitable market order.
role: Expose institutional mediation and feedback in economic regularities.

ideas.statement: Arithmetic limits, technology and efficiency gains leave distribution to contracts, bargaining and institutions.
Rewards can change measured relationships and social influence can amplify unequal outcomes without making either merit or chance the sole cause.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: A cultural-market experiment found social influence increased inequality and unpredictability while measured quality remained relevant.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: The artificial market is not a full theory of merit; denying constraints can evade responsibility as much as naturalizing advantage.
